bullets.text: Underwriting margin missed the 4% objective by 8.4 points in 2000; 5-year average underwriting profit margin was 3.2%; ROE fell to 1.7% from 10.9% in 1999, 16.7 points below target.

Total portfolio return was 8.6% (fixed-income 11.1%, duration 3.5 years; internal equities 1.1%); retired $300M in maturing debt; debt-to-capital reached 20.7%; repurchased 272,500 shares at $58.09 average.
Raised rates quickly to restore adequate pricing following PIP and physical damage cost spikes; 80% of policies shifted to six-month terms versus 35% in 1999 to speed rate-change impacts.
Premium volume grew 1% in 2000, missing the target of inflation plus 15 percentage points as rate increases reduced price competitiveness; 5-year average annual growth rate was 16%.

Agency expense ratio fell to 18.8% from 20.7%, aided by more renewals, lower Gainsharing, and removing brand advertising charges. Direct expense ratio dropped to 29.6% from 38.5% via better ad buying and renewals.

Unanticipated increases in personal injury protection and physical damage claim costs caused rate inadequacy; reserves were increased after concerns of deficiency arose, with a detailed reserve analysis publication planned.

Employee turnover escalated to 22.4% from 18.4% in 1999. The Gainsharing payout declined to $8.3 million from $55.6 million in 1999; Progressive reverted to its annual profit standard for 2000 and beyond.

Glenn reorganized functionally in April 2000, separating agent-produced and telephone/Internet business. Claims became a separate department reporting to Glenn, with a 16-person team to eliminate roadblocks to decision making and standard setting.
Internet business rose to 15% of Direct NPW (7% in 1999) and 3% of company volume (1% in 1999); won Gomez award for #1 online insurance carrier for three consecutive quarters.

Lewis concludes 35-year tenure as CEO, transitioning to Chairman as Glenn Renwick assumes CEO role; reiterates commitment to Core Values, the 4% underwriting profit objective, and transparently addressing operational shortfalls.
